title: Volume 1 Chapter 5: Skill Certification 3
content: The next day after school, while waiting for Sayori and the others in the garage, Sayori timidly walked in.
“Sayori, you weren’t like this before, were you?”
“B-but! We’re supposed to be banned from coming here! I came because Azuma-kun called me, but… it’s still awkward!”
“You were called, so come on in!”
“Wait, Karla! Don’t push me with your four arms!”
Karla forcibly pulled Sayori inside. Our eyes met as I waited.
“Ah… Azuma-kun, um, it’s been about ten days since we talked properly, right?”
“Yeah, it has. It feels like a while.”
I wasn’t sure if ten days counted as a long time, but compared to the almost daily meetings we had in the garage, it certainly felt like a while.
“Aren’t you and Sayori from the same school?”
“…Well, it’s because you don’t talk to me at school, Azuma-kun. And since I can’t come to the garage, I thought it might be a bother to reach out.”
“Oh, really? How old-fashioned.”
“What’s that supposed to mean!? Karla, why are you laughing?”
In stark contrast to Sayori, who looked clearly awkward, Karla appeared to be her usual self. It was hard to tell what she was thinking since she had a carefree personality.
“So—um, Azuma-kun, is something going on?”
“Yeah, I’m thinking of asking my dad if I can do nails in the garage.”
“Eh… but will he actually listen if you ask?”
I hadn’t talked about my father’s personality before, but after our conversations leading up to today, Sayori seemed to have picked up on the impression that he was a strict person.
“Yeah, so I’m going to change how I ask.”
“I’ve decided to seriously pursue getting my Nailist qualification.”
“Eh, really? That’s amazing!?”
For a moment, Sayori’s face lit up—only to quickly change to a look of confusion.
“…Huh? How does getting a qualification relate to using the garage?”

“It relates. The reason I’m doing nails here isn’t just for fun; it’s to get certified. I’ll borrow the garage for studying. The reason you and Karla are coming here is to help with that studying—so it’ll be framed that way.”
“…Oh? Oh?”
Sayori still seemed to struggle to understand what I meant, her eyes wide. Meanwhile, Karla began to smile mischievously.

“Ah, I see? You’re going to use the excuse that you want to get a qualification for the future, so you’re asking your father to lend you the garage? Parents can be weak to things like future plans and qualifications, right?”
“Well, saying weak might be misleading, but… I think he’ll be more willing to help if I say I want to study for a qualification.”
If I say I want to study for my future, it should be easier for my father to agree than if I just asked to borrow the space for a hobby.
“But, you know, the original problem was caused by the photos on SNS, right? That issue hasn’t been resolved.”
“Yeah. I had the posted photos deleted through Karla’s agency, but there are still risks. However, I’m thinking about that too.”

I showed them the smartphone site I used when I was taking model commissions. It was a mediation site. Although it charged fees, it safely delivered products—meaning the plastic models I made—to the clients.

This site also dealt with various skills sold and bought over the internet, from web design to video and animation, as well as songwriting. The most notable feature was that it didn’t matter whether the creator was a professional or an amateur.
If a client liked the creator’s past work, the transaction would be completed. That’s the kind of site it was.
I heard this was formally called a skill market.
“First, I’ll study for the Nailist Level 3 qualification. Then I’ll have my nail chips listed on this site.”
“Oh! So you’re going to become a Nailist through the web!?”
Karla exclaimed excitedly, waving her four arms.
“No, the chips I’ll be listing are just plastic ones—well, I’m just promoting that I can make nail chips as an extension of my model-making services.”
“Hmm? And then?”
“Even though it’s through the web, I’m doing this as a business—so if inquiries come to my father’s company, he can just pass along the site or my phone number.”
“Ah! So you’re creating a proper point of contact!”
Karla clapped her hands together, as if she finally understood. Her four arms moved so expressively that it was almost like she was dancing.
“Well, I don’t think I’ll get orders right away just because I got my Level 3 qualification. But I think this is the best way to convince my dad.”
“If you’re active as a creator on the web, it makes it easier to argue that you’re just borrowing the garage. Haha, you’ve thought this through, haven’t you, big brother?”
Karla grinned and leaned closer to me.
She even wrapped one of her arms around my shoulder from behind. Why is it that both Sayori and Karla get so close?
“Hey, I think it’s a good idea, you know? You’re a genius!”
“Stop praising me like that.”
That said, my father was fundamentally someone involved in making things. I believed that if I conveyed my passion for wanting to take the qualification and shape nails, he would surely understand.
“However, I can’t convey the beauty of nails alone. If Sayori and Karla, who have actually experienced my nails, are there, I think I could persuade my dad more effectively.”
“Of course! We’ll help persuade him together! Right, Sayori—”
Huh? Now that I think about it, Sayori, who would usually jump at this kind of conversation, was silent.
“Sayori?”
Karla called out with a worried tone. Sayori bit her lip without saying anything. Why does she have that expression? I thought she would be happy.
Tears began to spill from Sayori’s eyes.
“That’s not okay.”
“Eh?”
“That’s not okay, Azuma-kun.”
Wiping her tears with the sleeve of her uniform, Sayori shook her head.
“Eh? Huh? W-wait, Sayori?”
Karla flailed her four arms, confused about why Sayori was crying. I was just as lost. I thought this was a good idea, and if it meant getting the garage back, Sayori would surely be happy…
“Ah, is it that you don’t want me to post my nail works on the web? That’s right, you said you didn’t want to talk about me at school. But this is for the garage…”
“No, that’s not it, it’s not…”
Sayori, who was usually expressive with her emotions, seemed to be overflowing with tears that wouldn’t stop.
But—I never imagined that the girl I thought was perfect and completely different from me would cry like this.
“Plastic models…”
“Eh?”
“Azuma-kun, you haven’t been making plastic models lately, have you…?”
I was at a loss for words at Sayori’s unexpected statement.
“That’s my fault, isn’t it? Because I kept asking you for various nails, your time has been getting less and less… and you haven’t been able to make models, right?”
“Well, it’s true that I haven’t had time—”
“See!?”
Sayori burst into tears again.
Why are we talking about plastic models? I enjoy making models, so it shouldn’t be something for her to worry about.
“Sayori, calm down, let’s talk about this slowly, one thing at a time.”
“Y-yeah, okay…”
Karla took out a handkerchief and wiped Sayori’s eyes.
Sayori let out a sound that was more of a whimper than a cry.
“I’ve always been so happy. Finally being able to get my nails done. Having polish beautifully applied to my nails… Ah, if I asked Azuma-kun, he would shape any nail I wanted.”
Sniffling, Sayori continued to speak.

“I kept getting more and more excited, asking for this and that… I was so, so happy. Every time the color of my nails changed, I thought, ‘Is this really okay?’… But at the same time, I became just as anxious.”
“Anxious about what?”
“I was worried that by being so selfish, I was bothering you, Azuma-kun.”
Finally, it seemed her tears had calmed down a little.
With her eyes red and swollen, Sayori continued.
“And then, I realized something the other day. You haven’t been making models at all lately, just nails. When I asked you, you confirmed it…!”
“No, it’s because I enjoy doing it…!”
“Yeah, I know. What you love, I’ve taken away from you with my nails.”
—Is that so? Have I been so wrapped up in Sayori’s whims that I couldn’t spend time on what I loved?
“If I study for qualifications and become a proper Nailist… Ah, Azuma-kun, you won’t be able to make models at all! Because of me… that’s absolutely not okay!”
“Sayori…”
“I love the nails you do for me! I love them so much! But… I also loved hearing you talk about your models!”
Sayori started crying again.
With a tearful voice, she poured out what she had been holding back.

“I love nails too, so I totally understand how you feel! When you talked about models, your eyes sparkled, and you talked about everything so happily… I enjoyed listening to that! So I don’t want you to stop!”
I was at a loss for words.
It was true that I had always prioritized Sayori’s nails. I thought it was enough if I could make her happy by meeting her expectations.
But that convenience had made Sayori anxious.
“…When I heard that I couldn’t borrow the garage, honestly, I thought it was a chance.”
“A chance?”
Karla gently asked while hugging Sayori’s shoulders.
Karla truly was a good friend who cared for Sayori.
“Yeah—an opportunity to do nails without relying on Azuma-kun. I realized I could still do nails, so I thought I’d try on my own…”
I felt a bad premonition and quickly took Sayori’s hand.
“Ah, Azuma-kun…”
Sayori’s voice trembled with tears, but I didn’t care.
I firmly grasped Sayori’s hand and began to peel off the nail chips she had stuck on her nails, one by one.
The natural nails beneath the chips were in a pitiful state.
There were countless scratches on her nails, and the surface was uneven. On her middle finger, there was even a trace of blood.
She had been filing them down to that extent!
Karla gasped softly at the sight of her nails. It was a truly painful state.
“Ah, ahaha… you saw them.”
“Why… why are they in such terrible condition…!?”

“I bought a grinder or something and did it myself… It seems like I got a pretty powerful one, and, heh, I couldn’t do it as well as you, Azuma-kun… It’s pretty tough to do it with one hand, isn’t it?”
I was at a loss for words.
The reason she had been wearing nail chips wasn’t just for style. It was also to hide the fact that she had messed up filing her nails.
“So, you see? The reason I can’t use the garage is partly because of the SNS posts… From now on, I’ll try to do it on my own… and you’ll have time to make models, and it might be better that way…!”
“――――Don’t joke with me.”
The heat in my voice was stronger than I expected.
Sayori’s honesty had unleashed emotions I couldn’t hold back.
What swirled in my chest was a kind of anger.
“Ah, Azuma-kun?”
“That’s right. It’s all Sayori’s fault.”
“Ugh…”
“If it weren’t for Sayori, I would never have done nails. If Sayori hadn’t come to the garage every day, ordering this and that, I wouldn’t have researched nails this much to meet her requests.”
“Um, I’m sorry…”
Sayori looked like she was about to cry again.
“I would never have been interested in modeling work, and I wouldn’t have said it was okay to invite other friends. Everything, all of it, is Sayori’s fault.”
“W-wait, big brother, that’s too much…!”
Karla tried to intervene, but I couldn’t stop.
“So because of that—Sayori made me love nails this much.”
“Eh?”

“It’s fun to meet Sayori’s requests with my skills. I’m happy to express myself on her nails. Seeing Sayori happy with the nails I did made me genuinely happy—I had no idea nails could be this much fun.”
Sayori stared at me, mouth agape.
Did she think I was doing nails reluctantly? Just because she asked?
That couldn’t be further from the truth.
It was true that it all started because Sayori asked me. But…
“I was doing it because it was fun, because I wanted to do nails at that moment. It’s no different from when I make models. I’m just creating what I want to create, how I want to create it.”
“But what about plastic models…?”

“I’m just not prioritizing them right now. I’m assembling them when Sayori isn’t around. I have new models stacked in the back warehouse. I’m still slowly progressing with model commission requests. They’re just not my main focus right now, but I’m still making them when I want to.”
That’s right. I’ve always made what I wanted to make.
Whether it’s plastic models or nails, I’m essentially doing the same thing. It’s not about which is more important or prioritized.

“Learning new things and skills is fun. Studying for qualifications sounds enjoyable too. If I actually get certified, it’ll be even more fun. Once I get certified, opening a nail salon wouldn’t be a bad idea.”
I gently squeezed Sayori’s hand again.
I glared directly at her tear-streaked face.
It was Sayori who ignited my creative passion, and I would never allow her to run away from that.
“I want to do nails for Sayori because it’s fun for me.”
“So take responsibility and let me do your nails properly. I won’t allow these damaged nails—after all, it was you who first suggested it.”
Sayori stared at me for a while, her expression blank.
After pouring out everything I wanted to say, I regretted it. I had spoken purely based on my emotions.
Isn’t this a bit embarrassing?
“Ha… haha.”
“Sayori?”
“W-wait, what’s with that!? Haha, you’re asking to do my nails… that’s funny! Normally, it’s the other way around, right!? That’s too forceful! Ah, I can’t, this is too funny… ahahahaha!”
“It’s not forceful! I can’t do nails without your hands!”
I heard that hand models are needed for the certification exam.
The only person I can ask is Sayori, and if she starts saying she wants to do nails by herself, I’d be in trouble.
“Yeah… haha, that’s right. To do nails, you need my nails.”
“Of course.”
“I don’t want anyone else to do my nails but you, Azuma-kun! Yeah, it’s settled! I won’t worry about plastic models anymore! To continue doing nails here, let’s convince your dad together!”
Sayori seemed to have thought of something and released my hand.
“I still have about a hundred types of nails I want to get done!”
“That’s a lot.”
“Ahaha! It’s settled then! Didn’t you know? Girls are greedy!”
With her hands clasped behind her back, Sayori smiled bashfully.
I needed Sayori’s hands to do nails.
Sayori needed my hands to get her nails done.
“Um…”
As I thought about that,
Karla, half-lidded, looked at me while hugging Sayori.
“I’m sorry to interrupt your little moment, but I’m still here, you know? How long are you going to be lovey-dovey?”
“I-I’m not being lovey-dovey!”
Sayori denied it in a fluster.
—I hadn’t realized it, but since I had always been holding Sayori’s hand while doing her nails, I had no resistance to touching her hand.
This is bad, this is bad. The influence of nails is too strong.
“Big brother, you’re saying you have to take responsibility. That’s something a girl would normally say.”
“W-well, that’s not what I meant!”
“No, no, no, big brother. You don’t understand, do you? What it means for a girl to entrust her hands to someone?”
“Huh?”
Karla wore a teasing smile, the kind that made it clear she was about to poke fun at me.
“Hands and fingertips are a girl’s lifeline. If you’re going to entrust them to a boy from your class, it means you really like him and trust him a lot, you know?”
“A girl’s lifeline is her hair.”
“A girl has many important things that are as precious as her life!”
I thought that was a fallacy, but Karla was adamant.

“Listen! For a girl, nails are life! It’s self-expression! To entrust that to a boy from the same class, who isn’t a same-sex nail artist, and to let him mess with them, file them with something hard, and paint them in his color! That’s practically sex!”
“Wha!? No, that’s not right!”
What an outrageous thing for this blue-skinned girl to say!
“I trust you to the utmost, you know? Azuma-kun?”
Karla suddenly grabbed my hand with her four arms.
Damn it, I was firmly held by her four arms and couldn’t escape.
I was weaker than most guys to begin with.
“Stop! Don’t take Azuma-kun away!”
The dragon girl was on the verge of tears again. Sayori had been crying all day.
Since my hand was taken by Karla, Sayori instead wrapped her arms around my bicep.
Sayori was also strong, though not as much as Karla.
“Azuma-kun is my nail artist! He’s going to become a great Nailist! I’m his first and forever exclusive client! Right, Azuma-kun?”
“Uh, well…”
“Right! Right!”
“Y-yes…”
Under Sayori’s pressure, I found myself nodding without thinking.
I had been permanently designated as the dragon girl’s exclusive nail artist. However, I had just embarrassingly confessed that I “like nails.”
There was no way I could back out now.
“Geez, I can’t win against you.”
Karla, who had been teasing me, was surprisingly smiling happily.
She released my hand and shrugged her shoulders with her four arms. Even her casual gestures seemed to be exaggerated, as if she were dancing.
(I still don’t know if I can use the garage. But…)
Somehow, I felt that with these three around, I could do nails anywhere, not just in the garage. Because we trusted each other enough to feel comfortable handing over our hands.
So I was sure it would be okay.
Without any basis, I felt positively that way.
—I might have started to resemble Sayori a bit, being blindly optimistic.
